subject: biology-1
question: Meiosis has two divisions with different jobs. Which statement correctly matches each division to its role?

options.text: Meiosis I is equational because it splits replicated chromosomes into two cells without changing the chromosome number.
Meiosis I is the reductional division because homologous chromosomes separate, halving the chromosome number; meiosis II is the equational division because sister chromatids separate.
Both meiotic divisions reduce the chromosome number by half, first from 46 to 23 and then from 23 to about 12.
Meiosis II is the reductional division because it produces haploid cells, while meiosis I is equational.

explanation: The chromosome count drops from diploid to haploid in meiosis I, when homologs separate, so meiosis I is called the reductional division. Meiosis II separates sister chromatids much like mitosis and keeps the count at haploid, so it is the equational division. A and D swap the labels, and C misstates the count, which changes only once.
